post.text:
How to setup your Claude code project?

TL;DR

Most developers skip the setup and just start prompting. That's the mistake.

A proper Claude Code project lives inside a .𝗰𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲/ folder. Start with 𝗖𝗟𝗔𝗨𝗗𝗘.𝗺𝗱 as Claude's instruction manual. Split it into a 𝗿𝘂𝗹𝗲𝘀/ folder as it grows. Add 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗱𝘀/ for repeatable workflows, 𝘀𝗸𝗶𝗹𝗹𝘀/ for context-triggered automation, and 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁𝘀/ for isolated subagents. Lock down permissions in 𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀.𝗷𝘀𝗼𝗻.

There are two .𝗰𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲/ folders: one committed with your repo, one global at ~/.𝗰𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲/ for personal preferences and auto-memory across projects.

The .𝗰𝗹𝗮𝘂𝗱𝗲/ folder is infrastructure. Treat it like one.

The article below is a complete guide to 𝗖𝗟𝗔𝗨𝗗𝗘.𝗺𝗱, custom commands, skills, agents, and permissions, and how to set them up properly.

Yes, in Claude Code, slash commands were merged into skills (v2.1.3, Jan 2026). 

Existing .claude/commands/*.md files still work unchanged and appear as /slash commands. 

But skills (.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md) are now recommended—they add auto-invocation, subagents, extra files, and progressive disclosure. 

The original post's distinction is outdated; treat commands as legacy skills.

comments.text:
grok 帖子详细总结：教你用 .claude/ 文件夹搭建Claude代码项目基础设施。

核心结构：
- CLAUDE.md（团队指令，提交git）
- .claude/ 是控制中心：
 - settings.json（权限配置）
 - commands/（自定义斜杠命令，如 /project:review）
 - rules/（模块化规则：代码风格、测试等）
 - skills/（自动触发工作流）
 - agents/（子代理如代码审查员）

还有全局 ~/.claude/ 用于个人偏好。

你该怎么做：进入项目根目录，创建 .claude/ 文件夹，按图中结构添加文件，从 CLAUDE.md 开始写项目规则。

下一步行动：现在就新建 CLAUDE.md，填入你的团队指令和规范，测试一个自定义命令。

Takeaway：别直接乱prompt，把 .claude/ 当成Claude的“大脑基础设施”，让它变成结构化队友，大幅提升效率。

comments.text:
It's all good. And they all are necessary. But you can not depend on md files fully. 
I've been building with agents heavily since last summer. one thing is consistently true: the longer a development process goes, the more the agent loses track. Decisions from three sessions ago, architectural choices that seemed settled are gone. it starts making mistakes it wouldn't have made on day one.
I tried capturing context at session boundaries, at task completion, when decisions were made. None of it was reliable enough. The model misses things, events are ambiguous, "done" is never really a clear moment mid-session. The only thing that's always true is this: when you commit, something real happened. it's deterministic, it's intentional, it's a natural checkpoint in the workflow. So I built my open sourced platform Frame's context system around git commits instead. Pre commit hook updates the architecture map automatically, task state syncs from the commit, context gets captured at that exact moment. Everything else was too fuzzy. Git was already there, already reliable, already meaningful. So I suggest the same, just implement git to your agentic-development process. Or just look at it mine :).
I am always open to feedbacks and contributions. Actually I need them. I would be very happy.
Github : https://t.co/AtCAGPeWSh

comments.name: Slava Baranskyi, FCIM
comments.text: Solid breakdown. We took this a step further with OpenClaw. Same philosophy: CLAUDE.md is your source of truth, skills are modular, agents get isolated personas. But we added a layer on top: SOUL.md (who the agent is), MEMORY.md (what it remembers between sessions), and USER.md (who it's working for). The .claude folder is infrastructure. Agreed. But infrastructure without identity is just a tool. Give it memory and context, and it becomes a teammate.
